 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 & 227
 Of The Constitution Of India Praying To Issue Writ Of
 Certiorari Or Any Other Appropriate Writs Or Directions
 Quashing The Impugned Notice Dated 07/10/2023 Bearing
 No.A.Y/Raranv/P.R/183/2023-24 Issued By R4 Vide Annexure-E
 And Etc.
 This Writ Petition, Coming On For Further Hearing,
 This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order
1.  The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
a. Issue a writ of certiorari or any other appropriate writs or directions quashing the impugned notice dated 07.10.2023 bearing No. A.Y/RaRaNV/P.R/183/2023-24 issued by Respondent No.4 vide Annexure-E;
b. Issue writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writs or directions directing the Respondents herein to consider the Receipt filed by the petitioner herein for the New Trade Licence for the year 2022-23 vide Annexure-D;
Maltesh Paitl vs Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike on 29 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70981554/
2 c. Grant such other and further reliefs as this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to grant in the interest of justice and equity. 
NC: 2024:KHC:3742 d. Issue writ of Certiorari or any appropriate writs or directions setting aside the rejection order dated 28.10.2023 bearing application No.
N232419101163534 passed by the Health Officer (zonal)/Respondent No.5 vide Annexure-G produced along with this application. 
2. The petitioner claims to be engaged in the business of owning and operating cloud kitchens under brand name "Sharief Bhai" as regards which the petitioner has obtained licenses from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. The petitioner took on lease the ground floor of the premises bearing No.45 and 46 of Channa Sandra Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk-560061 measuring 1950 Sq.ft. for the purpose of running his business. A trade license for the said business having been applied for on 17.12.2022, Respondent No.5 on 7.10.2023 called upon the petitioner to vacate the premises, since the petitioner was using the basement parking as a kitchen. 
It is in that background that the petitioner had approached this Court seeking for the aforesaid reliefs. 
NC: 2024:KHC:3742 3. The standing counsel was directed to accept the notice for respondent on 12.10.2023. On 13.12.2023, a submission was made that the application filed by the petitioner had been rejected on the ground that in the basement a kitchen was being run. Hence, the counsel for the petitioner submitted that no such kitchen is being run but only certain items were stored and an affidavit of undertaking would be filed by the petitioner that the basement was not be used for any such purpose, such an affidavit came to be filed on 25.10.2023. 
4. Subsequently, the application filed by the petitioner allegedly came to be rejected on the grounds that the property is in a residential area. Hence, an amendment was carried out challenging the same, objections were also filed by the respondent. 
5. Initially it was contended by the corporation that the road width in front of the property of the petitioner was NC: 2024:KHC:3742 less than 40 feet and as such the no commercial activity could be carried out therein. Subsequently, it was contended that no permission from the fire forces had been obtained. In that view of the matter the Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Service Department represented by the Director General of Police and Director General of Fire and Emergency Services was brought on record as party respondent, since the BBMP was not in a position to place on record as to under what provision and what permission is required to be obtained. 
6. A report came to be filed enclosing notification dated 20.9.1971 by the learned AGA on behalf of the Fire Department. It was categorically stated that there is no permission which is required from the Fire Department except that certain of the guidelines were required to be followed by a restaurant. 
Maltesh Paitl vs Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike on 29 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70981554/
3 NC: 2024:KHC:3742 7. On that day, on instructions another submission was made by the learned counsel for respondent that the width of the road was less than 40 feet. Hence, the respondent was directed to carry out an inspection measure of the road in front of the property of the petitioner and file a report. The report to that effect has been filed along with a memo dated 19.1.2024 which now indicates that the road width is 21.20 mts. i.e., 70 feet and plot size is 464.69 sq. mtr. with a construction of five floors put up thereon. 
8. Sri. Sathayananda., learned counsel for BBMP would now submit that it is only 30% of the built up area which could be used for commercial purpose, since the property of the petitioner lies in ring 3 whereas the entire property has been used for commercial purpose. On enquiry as to why the width of the road has changed from time to time i.e., on first occasion it was submitted that the road width was less than 40 feet in so far as the petitioner in WP No.23065/2023 it has been NC:
2024:KHC:3742 submitted that the road width is 70 feet in so far as another petitioner in WP No.28108/2023 the road width is stated to be 19.40 mts. there is no particular explanation which is offered more so when both the property lie on the same road. 
9. The submissions made are contrary to the plan which has been sanctioned by the BBMP itself in as much as the plan which has been sanctioned in favor of the landlord of the petitioner indicates the road width is 24 mts. If that be so, it was not permissible on part of the respondent to make his submission initially that the road width was less than 40 feet now it is 70 feet when the plan itself indicates it to be 24 mtr road which is more than 70 feet. 
10. Apart therefrom, a perusal of the plan which has been sanctioned would indicate that the ground floor has been sanctioned for commercial purposes and it is only the upper floors which had been sanctioned for residential purposes. If that be so, the respondent- NC: 2024:KHC:3742 BBMP could have taken action only against the upper floors though granted for residential purposes are now allegedly being used for commercial purposes and no action could have been initiated against the petitioner who's plan sanction is for commercial purpose that is to say the ground floor has been sanctioned for commercial purpose and the extent of such sanction is also less than 30% of the total built up area. 
11. The manner in which the respondent officials have acted in the present matter would only indicate the disregard that they have for the rule of law, if not, for total absence of knowledge of applicable rules. There have been consistent efforts made to mislead this Court by initially stating that the road width is 40 feet and subsequent to the 70 feet when the plan which had been sanctioned by the BBMP itself would indicate that the road width is 24 mts and that the ground floor has been sanctioned for commercial purposes which is what the petitioner has put the said ground floor to use of. 
NC: 2024:KHC:3742 Maltesh Paitl vs Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike on 29 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70981554/
4 12. Further submission made that the notices have been issued to the landowner to make a choice as to which 30% of the property could be used for commercial purposes and balance to be used for residential purposes and in this regard the notice at page 19 to the memo dated 19.1.2024 is laid reference to which is dated 26.12.2023. A perusal thereof would indicate that the notice is addressed to the building owner of No.48, Srinivasapura Cross, Uttarahalli Main Road whereas plan sanctioned in favour of the petitioner is granted in respect of site No.16, BEML Employees Co-operative Societies Limited Sy.No.22/1, 22/6, 22/7 and 48 Channa Sandra Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk. The said notice dated 26.12.2023 does not even bear the name of the owner, when the respondent BBMP is in possession of the plan sanction showing the name of the owner, the Khatha certificate issued by the BBMP in the name of the owner and taxes are being collected in respect of said property. All - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:3742 details and documents being available with the Corporation, be it with another department, it is required of the officer issuing a notice to examine the same and then issue such notices, a notice for vacating and or demolition and or closure of business has civil consequences and cannot be so issued on assumptions and presumptions or the ipse dixit of the officer issuing such notice. There is a duty imposed on the person exercising power to examine the relevant facts and material before issuing such notice. 
13. Therefore, it appears to be a wanton attempt made by the officers of the Corporation to issue these kinds of notices against the petitioners contrary to the applicable law, more so when no such notice could have been issued when the ground floor of the building was sanctioned for commercial purposes and has been permitted to be used by BBMP for commercial purposes. Action if any, could have been initiated by the BBMP against the upper floor occupants/owners since those - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:3742 upper floors had been sanctioned for residential purposes. 
14. There being a wanton attempt made to mislead this Court, the Chief Commissioner is directed to take necessary action against the concerned officials who had brief Sri.Satyanand.B.S. in the matter and who have filed objections in the matter. 
15. It is expected of the State and/or its instrumentality to be a model litigant and place the true facts on record and not to try and mislead this Court. Though, such an attempt may be amenable to the contempt jurisdiction to this Court, this Court restrains from doing so, in view of the submission made by Sri.Satyanand.B.S.
16. That view of the matter, having been found that the sanctioned use of the property of the petitioner was for commercial use and it has been put to such use. The notices which have been issued by the respondents being contrary to the plan sanction in favour of the Maltesh Paitl vs Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike on 29 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70981554/
5 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:3742 landlord of the petitioner and contrary to the zonal regulations, I pass the following;
 ORDER i. The writ petition is allowed. 
ii. A certiorari is issued, the notice dated 7.10.2023  bearing No.A.Y/RaRaNV/P.R/183/2023-24 at  Annexure-E is hereby quashed. 
iii. A certiorari is issued, the rejection order dated 28.10.2023 passed by respondent No.5 at Annexure-G is hereby quash. 
iv. Respondent No.5 is directed consider the application made by the petitioner in terms of the plan sanction granted by the respondent considering the property of the petitioner to be sanctioned for commercial purposes and issue necessary trade license within a period of 15 days from today.
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:3742 v. Sri.Satyanand.B.S. is directed to inform the respondent No.5 about the above order.

summary.facts:
A trade license for the said business having been applied for on 17.12.2022, Respondent No.5 on 7.10.2023 called upon the petitioner to vacate the premises, since the petitioner was using the basement parking as a kitchen.
On 13.12.2023, a submission was made that the application filed by the petitioner had been rejected on the ground that in the basement a kitchen was being run.
Hence, the counsel for the petitioner submitted that no such kitchen is being run but only certain items were stored and an affidavit of undertaking would be filed by the petitioner that the basement was not be used for any such purpose, such an affidavit came to be filed on 25.10.2023.
4. Subsequently, the application filed by the petitioner allegedly came to be rejected on the grounds that the property is in a residential area.
Hence, an amendment was carried out challenging the same, objections were also filed by the respondent.
5. Initially it was contended by the corporation that the road width in front of the property of the petitioner was NC: 2024:KHC:3742 less than 40 feet and as such the no commercial activity could be carried out therein.
In that view of the matter the Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Service Department represented by the Director General of Police and Director General of Fire and Emergency Services was brought on record as party respondent, since the BBMP was not in a position to place on record as to under what provision and what permission is required to be obtained.

6. A report came to be filed enclosing notification dated 20.9.1971 by the learned AGA on behalf of the Fire Department.
It was categorically stated that there is no permission which is required from the Fire Department except that certain of the guidelines were required to be followed by a restaurant.
summary.ANALYSIS:
11. The manner in which the respondent officials have acted in the present matter would only indicate the disregard that they have for the rule of law, if not, for total absence of knowledge of applicable rules.
There is a duty imposed on the person exercising power to examine the relevant facts and material before issuing such notice.
14. There being a wanton attempt made to mislead this Court, the Chief Commissioner is directed to take necessary action against the concerned officials who had brief Sri.Satyanand.B.S. in the matter and who have filed objections in the matter.
15. It is expected of the State and/or its instrumentality to be a model litigant and place the true facts on record and not to try and mislead this Court.
That view of the matter, having been found that the sanctioned use of the property of the petitioner was for commercial use and it has been put to such use.
